html:
The Aden Emergency was the revolt against British rule in Aden and its hinterland from 1963 to 1967. It began with a grenade attack on the British high commissioner in December 1963.

Two nationalist groups, the National Liberation Front and a rival backed by Egypt, fought the British and each other. Britain announced it would leave, and its last troops sailed on 29 November 1967. The National Liberation Front took power.

The new state became the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen, or South Yemen, the only Marxist state in the Arab world, allied to the Soviet Union. It armed rebels in Oman's Dhofar. It was joined with the north in unification in 1990. See also British Aden.
